title: Containers for Change (Queensland)
summary: Queensland's container refund scheme, Containers for Change, began on 1 November 2018 with a 10-cent refund and more than 230 refund points.

instruments.title: Waste Reduction and Recycling Amendment Act 2017

direction_rationale: Beverage suppliers must register containers and pay per-container scheme costs, a compliance cost that weighs more on small and interstate producers/importers (potential barrier and price effect), while new refund-point and materials-recovery businesses enter.

industries.name: Soft Drink, Cordial and Syrup Manufacturing
Wine and Other Alcoholic Beverage Manufacturing
Waste Remediation and Materials Recovery Services

comparison: States without a scheme at the time (staggered adoption NT 2012 to TAS 2025; SA since 1977 always treated)
confounders: plastic bag bans in the same period
beverage excise and alcohol tax changes
Queensland lightweight plastic bag ban 1 Jul 2018
price_series: Waters, soft drinks and juices; Beer

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Beverage suppliers fund a 10-cent refund on containers. It prices litter and waste more fully, but each state runs its own scheme, with its own registration and costs, which weighs most on small and interstate suppliers.

marks.reason: Suppliers must register every container type and report and pay scheme costs.
Each state's scheme has its own registration and cost recovery, adding costs to selling in several states.
The deposit puts a price on littered and landfilled containers, a cost the market otherwise ignores.
